candidate.why_underserved: Every hosted ESP monetizes per stored contact, so no incumbent will fix the incentive; the self-hosted escape hatches filter out exactly the non-technical owners who complain loudest. A dead-simple flat-price app with bring-your-own SMTP/SES, where unsubscribed contacts cost nothing by design, is structurally off-limits to incumbents.
candidate.willingness_to_pay_signal: Users pay $45-300+/mo and can quantify the waste ($180+/yr on unsubscribed-contact billing alone); one analysis found 418 users publicly leaving Mailchimp Nov 2025-Feb 2026. Single-digit monthly or flat pricing is an easy calculation.
candidate.rationale: Found by two researchers independently; the Dec 2025 free-plan cut re-ignited the complaint wave, so timing is hot. BYO sending credentials means zero paid APIs for the founder. Docked slightly on buildability nuance: deliverability hand-holding (DNS, warmup) is real support burden, and 'help non-technical users configure SES' is the hidden hard part. Still a clear structural wedge no incumbent can copy.

verification.evidence_check: Direct fetches of all 4 cited URLs were blocked by the sandbox proxy (403 CONNECT denials), so each was verified via web search instead. (1) productiveblogging.com/unsubscribed-contacts-mailchimp/ — VERIFIED: real page, teaches archiving unsubscribed contacts to stop paying for them; pain matches. (2) saasprices.net free-plan-nerf post — could not load directly, but the underlying claim is independently corroborated by beehiiv.com, emailexpert.com, and groupmail.io: free plan cut to 250 contacts/500 sends (sources date the final cut to Jan 2026, not Dec 2025 — minor discrepancy), classic automations removed from free plan June 2025. (3) 5forests.com 'Tired of paying for non-subscribers' — VERIFIED: real agency post about winery clients paying for non-subscribed contacts. (4) digitalsproductivity.com '247 Users Share Real Costs' — page exists and contains the claimed content, but it is a low-credibility AI-content-farm-style site (title says 'DigitalEdgeLab' on a domain called digitalsproductivity.com; the '247 threads / 1,847 responses' methodology is unverifiable). The '418 users publicly leaving Nov 2025–Feb 2026' WTP figure in the hypothesis traces to this dubious source and should not be trusted. Net: the core pain (Mailchimp bills for unsubscribed/non-subscribed contacts; free plan repeatedly gutted) is real and well-documented, including in Mailchimp's own help docs.
verification.competitor_check: This is where the hypothesis collapses. The claim that 'every hosted ESP monetizes per stored contact, so no incumbent will fix the incentive' is factually false: (a) MailerLite — hosted, well-loved (4.6+ ratings), free to 500 subs/12k emails, ~$10/mo at 1k subs, and unsubscribed/bounced contacts explicitly do NOT count toward billing (confirmed in MailerLite's own billing docs). (b) EmailOctopus — hosted, cheap, unsubscribed contacts do NOT count toward the plan limit (confirmed in their help docs). (c) Brevo — no per-contact billing at all: unlimited contacts, pay per email sent, from $9/mo for 5k emails; comparison articles cite 25k-contact Mailchimp users cutting $170/mo to $29/mo. (d) Kit (ConvertKit) — FREE up to 10,000 subscribers with unlimited sends, which single-handedly covers most of the hypothesized 250–20k segment. (e) beehiiv — free to 2,500 subscribers, purpose-built for newsletters/creators. (f) The exact hypothesized product already exists hosted: MailBluster — cloud-hosted, BYO Amazon SES/Postmark/Mailgun/SMTP2GO, unlimited contacts at no extra charge, free starter tier, Pro at $5/mo ($60/yr) + $0.60/1,000 emails. BigMailer is another hosted BYO-SES player (free under 1,000 contacts, ~$20/mo to 20k). (g) Sendy — $69 one-time self-hosted BYO-SES, hugely popular with the semi-technical. The 'structurally off-limits to incumbents' wedge does not exist; unsubscribed-cost-nothing billing is already mainstream outside Mailchimp.
verification.demand_check: Independent evidence that the PAIN is real is abundant: Mailchimp's own docs confirm subscribed/unsubscribed/non-subscribed all count toward billing; emailtooltester, retainful, justpricing, benchmarkemail, sendx, and emailvendorselection all flag it as a hidden cost in 2026; one 2026 analysis of r/MailChimp states the unsubscribed-contact mechanic is 'the most common reason established businesses switch platforms'; beehiiv and emailexpert independently covered the free-plan shrink to 250 contacts. However, the demand expresses itself as 'leave Mailchimp for an existing cheaper tool' — documented switch destinations are MailerLite ('cut costs 60%'), Brevo, EmailOctopus, and Kit — NOT as unmet demand for a new flat-price BYO-SES app. Evidence of willingness to pay for the specific hypothesized product is weak: MailBluster already sells nearly exactly this for $5/mo and remains a niche player, suggesting BYO-SES setup (AWS account, sandbox exit, DNS/DKIM) is a real adoption barrier for the non-technical audience the hypothesis targets — the same barrier the hypothesis itself flags as the 'hidden hard part'.
verification.fatal_flaws: 1) The core 'why_underserved' premise is refuted: MailerLite and EmailOctopus don't bill for unsubscribed contacts, and Brevo/MailBluster don't bill per contact at all — hosted incumbents HAVE fixed the incentive. 2) Kit's free 10,000-subscriber tier and beehiiv's free 2,500 tier blanket the exact 250–20k creator/author/nonprofit segment at $0. 3) The hypothesized product already exists (MailBluster $5/mo hosted BYO-SES unlimited contacts; BigMailer; Sendy $69 one-time), and none has broken out — the target user who can't self-host listmonk also can't comfortably exit the AWS SES sandbox, so the BYO-SES design filters out its own market. 4) The strongest quantified WTP datapoint (418 public leavers, '247 users' survey) comes from an unverifiable AI-content-farm source. 5) The remaining differentiation vs MailerLite/Brevo is a few dollars a month, against their brand trust, deliverability reputation, and free migration tooling.

candidate.title: UK landlord Making Tax Digital record-keeper: keep your spreadsheet workflow, file quarterly to HMRC
candidate.who: UK private landlords with >£50k rental income (~900k people mandated since April 2026; the >£30k wave hits April 2027), mostly self-managing 1-10 properties from Excel
candidate.pain_description: Since April 2026 these landlords must keep digital records and file quarterly HMRC updates; spreadsheets are only legal with fiddly 'digital link' bridging software. July 2026 surveys show ~13 hours/month on tax admin, 22% considering quitting the rental market over the burden, 59% fearing penalties, and the alternatives are £300-800/yr extra accountant fees or subscription SaaS that takes custody of their data.

evidence.quote: Almost a quarter of landlords ready to quit the rental market over Making Tax Digital burden
Landlords now spend an average of 13 hours a month – more than a day and a half of work – managing tax and financial admin.
businesses moving to MTD will incur around £280 to £350 in transitional costs, along with ongoing annual costs of around £115

candidate.existing_solutions: Accountants (£300-800/yr extra for quarterly support), Landlord Studio/Hammock/Landlord Vision (cloud subscriptions holding the data), Xero/QuickBooks (overkill, not per-property), clunky VAT-era bridging retrofits. 39% still on spreadsheets/manual methods.
candidate.why_underserved: Incumbent MTD tools demand data custody; landlords explicitly want to keep their own records. A landlord-native, local-first record keeper with per-property income categorisation plus HMRC quarterly submission (the MTD Income Tax API is free — developer registration, not a paid API) is a thin, well-defined wedge. Timing is exceptional: mandation began 3 months ago, next wave April 2027 grows the market.
candidate.willingness_to_pay_signal: Landlords value the admin time at £3,000+/yr, face £280-350 transitional costs and £300-800/yr accountant quotes; dozens of paid tools on HMRC's recognised-software list validate the budget. £50-150/yr undercuts everything.
candidate.rationale: The only candidate with a government-enforced forcing function — demand is compulsory, dated, and expanding. Free API, clear buyer, evergreen quarterly recurrence. Docked for: crowded HMRC-recognised list (validated but contested), HMRC recognition/integration process eating into the one-month window, and tax-domain correctness stakes. Evidence is trade-press/survey rather than raw first-person rants.

verification.evidence_check: Direct fetches of all three cited URLs were blocked by the sandbox proxy (403 CONNECT denial at the gateway, affecting all external hosts including example.com — a tooling limitation, not evidence the pages are dead). Verified indirectly via web search instead: (1) bdcmagazine.com article exists with the exact cited title and its content is corroborated — a Landlord Studio study claims 22% of landlords have considered leaving the rental market over MTD burden. (2) lettingagenttoday.co.uk article exists; the '13 hours a month — more than a day and a half of work — managing tax and financial admin' quote appears verbatim in search results, plus £3,000/yr time valuation and 36% fearing errors/penalties (the hypothesis's '59% fearing penalties' did not surface; closest verified figure is 36-38% for record-keeping/penalty concerns). (3) anna.money page exists and its £280-350 transitional / ~£115 ongoing figures match HMRC's own published estimates (£285 transitional/£115 ongoing for >£50k landlords; £350/£110 for the £30-50k band, per gov.uk). MAJOR CAVEAT: the headline pain stats (22% quitting, 13 hrs/month) come from a survey by Landlord Studio — a vendor selling landlord accounting software with an obvious interest in dramatizing the pain. Also, MTD-for-ITSA mandation from April 2026 (>£50k) and April 2027 (>£30k) is confirmed real via gov.uk and LITRG.
verification.competitor_check: The exact proposed wedge — 'keep your spreadsheet workflow, file quarterly to HMRC' — is the literal definition of MTD bridging software, an established and well-loved category with live Income Tax products in 2026: 123 Sheets (£19.50+VAT/yr, FIVE-STAR average across 1,900+ Trustpilot reviews, has a dedicated landlords product page), VitalTax (£30-36/yr Excel add-in, 4.0 Trustpilot, HMRC-recognised for ITSA quarterly updates, adjustments and final declaration), GoFile (£49.99+VAT/yr for self-employment + property). The 'clunky VAT-era retrofits' framing in the hypothesis is outdated — these have purpose-built ITSA offerings. On top of that, HMRC's recognised list has 20+ genuinely FREE options including landlord-specific ones: RentalBux Free (all three MTD income types, free until March 2028), QuickFile (free to 1,000 ledger entries), Clear Books Free, TaxNav, FreeAgent (free via NatWest/Mettle banking). Landlord-native SaaS: Landlord Studio GO is FREE for the first 3 units (covering much of the '1-10 property' target), Hammock £8/mo (1-3 properties), Landlord Vision. The proposed £50-150/yr price sits ABOVE the segment's actual clearing price of £0-36/yr. The 'data custody / local-first' differentiator is hollow: with bridging software the landlord's own spreadsheet IS the digital record and stays on their machine — custody already stays with the landlord.
verification.demand_check: Independent evidence the pain is real: LandlordZone reports 'nearly 9 in 10 landlords anxious over digital tax shake-up' (separate from the cited articles); an OpenRent community forum thread 'Making Tax Digital from April 2026 — how are you preparing?' shows organic landlord discussion; Blick Rothenberg and LITRG document rising compliance risk, the points-based penalty regime (£200 fine at 2 points), and confusion about what digital record-keeping means; Parliament's Public Accounts Committee has criticized MTD's cost burden on taxpayers. Willingness to pay is confirmed but LOW-PRICED: HMRC itself estimates only ~£115/yr ongoing cost per mandated landlord, the most popular spreadsheet-bridging tools charge £20-36/yr, and multiple credible free options exist — so the compulsory demand is real, but the market has already priced this job at roughly a quarter to zero of the hypothesis's £50-150/yr target.
verification.fatal_flaws: 1) The 'underserved wedge' is a mischaracterization: spreadsheet-preserving MTD filing is a mature category (bridging software) with a 5-star, £19.50/yr incumbent (123 Sheets) and 20+ free HMRC-recognised alternatives — the hypothesis's own differentiators (keep your data, keep your spreadsheet, thin filing layer) are exactly what these deliver today. 2) Pricing is inverted: £50-150/yr does not 'undercut everything'; it is 2-5x the going rate for the target segment and infinitely more than the free tiers (Landlord Studio GO free for 3 units, RentalBux free to 2028). 3) The most dramatic evidence (22% quitting, 13 hrs/month) is a competitor vendor's marketing survey, not neutral data. 4) HMRC recognition is a gating process that must complete before a single sale, in a market where 40+ products are already listed and search/SEO channels are saturated by incumbents and affiliate listicles. The pain is genuine and government-enforced, but the specific gap this startup claims to fill closed before it opened.
